turns.zh: 是的。所以如果你像成吉思汗那样逐步升级，你可能会经历眼镜、电动汽车、机器人和脑机接口。

turns.en: Maybe based on what I know today, but as I learn maybe the idea changes, roadmap changes.
turns.zh: 也许基于我今天所知，但随着我学习，想法可能会改变，路线图也会改变。

turns.en: One of your investors said that you are really influenced by Eastern philosophy and Zen. I wondered where that came from for you and how maybe that influences how you think about what you're building.
turns.zh: 你的一位投资者说你深受东方哲学和禅宗的影响。我想知道这对你来说是从哪里来的，以及它可能如何影响你对自己所构建的东西的思考。

turns.en: In periods of my life when I was down, I took to philosophy quite a lot.
turns.zh: 在我人生低谷的时候，我大量接触了哲学。

turns.en: Both, I think Stoicism had a big impact on me, and then I also read a book that Steve Jobs read on Zen Buddhism. That was pretty interesting. So I guess the common thread is just to be more relaxed about things, see the bright side, and don't try to control what you can't control, but control what you can. So if there's something that doesn't work and you have no ability to influence it, just let it go.
turns.zh: 两者都有，我认为斯多葛主义对我影响很大，然后我也读了乔布斯读过的一本关于禅宗的书，那本书挺有意思的。所以我觉得共同点就是遇事更放松一些，看到事物积极的一面，不要试图控制你无法控制的东西，而是控制你能控制的。所以如果有些事情行不通，而你无法影响它，那就放手吧。

turns.en: Well, let's wrap up with maybe two philosophical or thought-experimenty questions. Oh, by the way, in middle school, philosophy was the class where I paid the most attention.
turns.zh: 好，我们最后再聊两个哲学或思想实验式的问题吧。哦，顺便说一句，中学时哲学课是我最专注的课。

turns.en: Ah, interesting. That's great that your middle school had philosophy. I think that's a great idea.
turns.zh: 啊，有意思。你们中学有哲学课，那太好了。我觉得这是个很棒的主意。

turns.en: If you had unlimited resources and no operational constraints, what's an experiment you would really like to run?
turns.zh: 如果你拥有无限的资源，没有任何运营限制，你真正想做的实验是什么？

turns.en: If that were the case, we would just do all the products we talked about just now, and then have the operating system integrate all of them, and spend a lot of resources on building a great brand that people love and increasing our retail distribution.
turns.zh: 如果是那样的话，我们就会把我们刚才谈到的所有产品都做出来，然后让操作系统把它们整合起来，并投入大量资源打造一个人们喜爱的伟大品牌，扩大我们的零售分销。

turns.en: If you could assign a book to everyone on Earth to read and understand, what would you want to assign?
turns.zh: 如果你能指定一本书让地球上的每个人都读并理解，你会指定哪一本？

turns.en: Philosophically, I don't really like to force people to learn, because I think it's okay to not learn. You're not a better person just because you learn stuff. But it's also your own responsibility to learn. Even if somebody really pushes you hard and you kind of don't want to do it, it's up to you.
turns.zh: 从哲学上讲，我不太喜欢强迫人们学习，因为我觉得不学习也没关系。你不会因为学了东西就成为一个更好的人。但学习也是你自己的责任。即使有人非常用力地推你，而你不太想做，那也是你自己的事。

turns.en: You think learning is totally morally neutral?
turns.zh: 你认为学习在道德上是完全中性的吗？

turns.en: It's a morally positive thing, but forcing people to do it is not a good thing. And everybody has their own responsibility to learn and get better. So for instance, when it comes to talent, I believe that talent is selected and not taught. You know what I mean? Like the people who learn, they're always going to learn irrespective of where they are, and you just select them, promote them. If you don't want to learn, even if I buy a very expensive course for you, you're still not going to learn.
turns.zh: 学习在道德上是积极的事情，但强迫人们学习不是好事。每个人都有责任学习和进步。比如，谈到人才，我相信人才是被选出来的，而不是教出来的。你明白我的意思吗？那些愿意学习的人，无论在哪里都会学习，你只需要选择他们、提拔他们。如果你不想学，即使我为你买一门非常昂贵的课程，你依然不会学。

turns.en: Yes.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: So I don't know what book people should read. Whatever makes you happy. I read a book on Provence, like living the good life in Provence. That was pretty relaxing.
turns.zh: 所以我不知道人们应该读什么书。让你开心的就好。我读了一本关于普罗旺斯的书，比如在普罗旺斯过美好生活。那本书很让人放松。

turns.en: Yeah. Amazing. Well, that feels like a great place to end. I'm really glad we had this chance to chat, and I think what you're building is extremely cool. And I can't wait to watch what happens next.
turns.zh: 是的。太棒了。好，这感觉是个很好的结束点。我很高兴我们有这次机会聊天，我觉得你在做的事情非常酷。我迫不及待想看看接下来会发生什么。

turns.en: Awesome. Thank you for the opportunity.
turns.zh: 太好了。谢谢你的邀请。

consensus.en: Tech products are becoming homogeneous; design is the fastest way to differentiate in mature categories.
consensus.zh: 科技产品日趋同质化；在成熟品类中，设计是差异化的最快方式。

consensus.en: Long-term vision: make tech fun to inspire human creativity, which is key to human competitiveness.
consensus.zh: 长期愿景：让科技变得有趣以激发人类创造力，这是人类竞争力的关键。

consensus.en: Marketing is about arbitrage and efficiency; find undervalued channels before they become crowded.
consensus.zh: 营销关乎套利和效率；在渠道变得拥挤之前找到被低估的渠道。

consensus.en: India is a huge opportunity for smartphones due to high Android market share and growing middle class.
consensus.zh: 印度是智能手机的巨大机遇，因为安卓市场份额高且中产阶级不断壮大。

consensus.en: AI should be an ingredient for better user experience, not a hype topic; focus on utility.
consensus.zh: AI 应是提升用户体验的要素，而非炒作话题；应聚焦实用性。

consensus.en: Community involvement keeps the company humble and true to its mission.
consensus.zh: 社区参与让公司保持谦逊并忠于使命。

contrarian.en: Retirement is boring; working is more relaxing than an extended holiday.
contrarian.zh: 退休很无聊；工作比长假更让人放松。

contrarian.en: Genghis Khan is a model entrepreneur due to his talent scouting and cultural openness.
contrarian.zh: 成吉思汗是企业家典范，因为他善于发掘人才且文化开放。

contrarian.en: In a mature category, focus on differentiation, not product-market fit.
contrarian.zh: 在成熟品类中，应聚焦差异化，而非寻找产品市场契合。

contrarian.en: Use an uncapped note for hardware startups to avoid dilution.
